newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shares close lower after corrections.
newsitem.headline: Lima shares close lower after corrections.

text.p: Lima shares dropped slightly Monday, due to technical corrections in the majority of sectors, brokers said.
Analysts expect the market to maintain that tendency Tuesday, especially in the polymetallic sector, which registered high gains in previous weeks because of the rising price for zinc.
According to preliminary figures, the Lima Stock Exchange's general index dropped 1.6 percent to 2,227.29 points, and the blue-chip selective index also fell 1.73 percent to 3,211.29 points.
Overall, $15.9 million was traded in 2,157 transactions as 37 shares fell, 16 rose and 21 remained stable.

"This is normally a very volatile month for the bolsa," said Jorge Gutierrez from brokerage Coril. "The mid-year account balances are due, there is the presidential address during the independence holidays and companies sell because of their need to pay salaries and bonuses."
He added that current political factors could affect investors, especially locally, who feel instability will affect their investments.

ING Baring analyst Jose Luis Cueto said that, although the political situation, including growing opposition to President Alberto Fujimori, was a potentially negative factor for Peru's foreign investors, "while the economic situation of this country is good, there are no major problems."

Despite low expectations for Tuesday, brokers were recommending that investors maintain positions in the brewery and construction sectors. They are expected to benefit from the emerging climatic phenomenon, El Nino, characterized by high temperatures on the coast and floods and damage in the north.
Winners Monday included miner Volcan, up 10 percent to 15.95 soles, electrical company Edelnor, up 0.51 percent to 1.96 soles, and cement-maker Cementos Lima, up 0.48 percent to 6.25 soles.
Volcan rose after the announcement that it was among the only three competing Friday for the purchase of the Mahr Tunel mining unit, whose minimum bidding price is $50 million.
The other two competitors are Peruvian miner Morococha and Sweden's Boliden.
Losers today included miner Perubar, off 7.57 percent at 8.30, miner Morococha, off 5.01 percent to 9.49 soles, and brewer Unin de Cerveceras Backus, off 2.8 percent to 2.43 soles.
Polymetallic miners lost ground even though the zinc reached a new high at $1.498 per ton, due to technical adjustments, brokers said.
Market leader Telefnica del Per "B" fell 0.71 percent to 6.95 soles.
